svg.text: ACM · how the model sees its own action
Action–Consequence Model, built on the Meaning Language Model. One action, many worlds, each with its own laws. Generated from a real run - nothing hand-placed.
impact spreads to each world by proximity
🏛️ society · economy world · economic · legal · social laws
instead of a new one being
desired outcome: pay my debt → ENABLED ➕
every node of every action graph is stored as a vector
83 dims: kind | role | entity type | circle | lemma hash | certainty · polarity · tense
cosine similarity of action nodes across stored graphs
John sold his car to Sarah.
The engineer deleted the database in production.
two nodes are close when they play the same part in
similar actions. A learned embedder can replace the
hashing one behind the same interface.

proximity: the actor's action spreads its impact outward, world by world, and a consequence can also flow back · ∿ synchronicity: worlds change together, down to the quantum level (correlation, not cause) · both are concepts, not yet modelled

red dummy = the origin actor, red vector = its action (dashed: reaches that actor only through its consequences) · blue dummies = the other actors, blue vectors = their reactions: the consequence for their goal, from the engine; what they do next is not predicted here
Ring → world: the rule engine places each consequence on a ring; the world named on each ring is an explicit mapping for this picture, not engine output.
scenario · context: Mark wants to buy my car. Sarah needs a car. · action: I will sell my car to Sarah in Paris tomorrow to pay my debt.
